# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 23 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 23 | **Condition:** fragmentary

---

**1** [...] I give You thanks, O Lord, for You have rescued my life from the pit,

**2** [...] and from the deepest abyss You have lifted me to an eternal summit,

**3** [...] and I walk across an endless expanse, and I know there is hope

**4** [...] for the one You shaped from dust to sit in Your eternal council.

**5** You purified my corrupt spirit from terrible sin,

**6** so I could take my place in the assembly alongside the holy ones,

**7** and join in fellowship with the heavenly congregation.

**8** You gave a mortal an everlasting inheritance among the spirits who know You,

**9** to celebrate Your name with shouts of joy and proclaim Your wonders before all creation.

**10** [...] But who am I — a creature made of clay? Something kneaded from water — why should I matter?

**11** [...] yet You lifted me up, and You placed [...] and I have come to know [...]

**12** [...] that righteousness belongs to Your truth, and [...] to Your faithful love [...]

**13** [...] and I have leaned hard on Your mercy, and [...] because You did not [...]

**14** [...] let me be destroyed by my own guilt, because You hold me up [...]

**15** [...] and You gave me insight into Your truth, and into Your hidden purposes [...]

**16** [...] You let me see, and into Your astonishing secret [...] You have [...]

**17** [...] in Your presence my steps are sure, and [...] against the wicked [...]

**18** [...] and You made my heart strong in Your covenant, and my feet [...]

**19** [...] stand firm on solid rock, and [...] the ancient paths [...]

**20** [...] there is hope for anyone You have turned back from sin, and [...]

**21** [...] You did not abandon me in [...] and You kept me going [...]

**22** [...] my life from ruin, and [...] surrounded by lions [...]

**23** [...] sent against the guilty, lions that shatter bones [...]

**24** [...] of the strong, and they drink the blood of [...] warriors [...]

**25** [...] and You raised me as a banner for those chosen for righteousness,

**26** [...] and as a wise revealer of astonishing secrets, to put to the test [...]

**27** [...] the truthful, and to refine those who welcome correction [...]

**28** [...] but to those who spread lies I am an opponent [...]

**29** [...] and a peacemaker to all who recognize truth [...]

**30** [...] Your name is [...] forever, and [...] for all time [...]

**31** [...] and by Your glory my light has blazed out, for You are a light [...]

**32** [...] that pierces through darkness, and [...] bringing healing [...]

**33** [...] and amazing strength to the one who [...] and an everlasting sign [...]

**34** [...] forever [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 23 is one of the most emotionally powerful passages in the Hodayot. The movement from pit to heavenly assembly, from clay to angelic fellowship, captures the essence of Qumran spirituality. The lion imagery evokes both danger and divine protection. Rendered dynamically to let modern readers feel the same devotional intensity the Qumran worshiper experienced.*
